Subject: Follow-up: data residency & region pinning (post-call recap)

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

What I heard:
- Primary requirement: customer data (PII and model inputs) must be stored and processed inside US regions for production workloads.
- Non-prod (dev/staging) can be in other regions but must be clearly segregated.
- Cross-region failover should be limited and require approval; backups must be encrypted and stored in the US.
- Strong interest in audit logs, retention settings (30/90/365 day options), and the ability to purge on request.

Clarifying questions we flagged on the call (can you confirm?):
1) Do you need region pinning at a per-environment level (prod vs non-prod) or per-application/team?
2) For cross-region failover: acceptable RTO/RPO targets and whether automatic failover is allowed or only manual with approvals?
3) Any regulatory constraints around backups (e.g., backups cannot leave the US under any circumstances)?
4) Who from legal/infosec should we include for the technical deep-dive?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I can set up a 60-min tech deep-dive (engineers + infra) to map region pinning options and failover behavior.
- We'll attach the short data-residency questionnaire so your security team can capture requirements (see attachment).
- I'll pull in Aditya (technical PM) and Marissa (solutions lead) to confirm implementation patterns and provide a short note on retention / purge workflows.

Proposed times: Mon 6/22 10am PT or Tue 6/23 2pm PT — tell me which works and who from your side will attend.

Attachment: acme-data-residency-questions.xlsx (questionnaire)

Thanks,

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and clarifications below.

1) Region pinning: We need prod pinned to US (primary) at the account level. Some lines of business may want per-app controls — we can surface those in the questionnaire.
2) Failover: We prefer manual failover with formal approval from our on-call/SRE lead. Automatic cross-region failover is acceptable only for predefined outage classes. RTO target for prod is <= 15 minutes; RPO <= 5 minutes.
3) Backups: All backups must be stored within US-only regions. Encrypted at rest, customer-managed KMS preferred.
4) Legal/Infosec: Please loop in our data-protection lead, Sara Miller (sara.miller@acmebank.com). I’ve cc'd legal.

We've attached the filled questionnaire for a couple of initial items and flagged the items where we need architecture diagrams. Will the whitepaper you mentioned cover failover options and how Redwood handles regional failover and backups?

Also — what are typical audit log retention defaults and can we get granular per-application retention policies?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Sr. Product Manager — Data Platforms
Acme Bank

4) KMS/Backups: We support customer-managed KMS for both primary and backup snapshots; backups can be restricted to US regions only.
